title: Vertical slice locality vs strict horizontal layering
task: Review a proposal to move a small feature from a cohesive vertical slice into global controller/service/repository directories solely for consistency with a layering template.
context: The feature has one endpoint, one use-case module, one persistence query, and feature-specific tests.
No other feature reuses the use-case logic.
The current slice keeps feature code physically close.
Dependency direction is already one-way and explicit.
The proposed horizontal move does not create a shared invariant or provider boundary.
evidence: Current imports do not violate architectural dependency direction.
The proposed move increases navigation across four directories.
No shared service/repository abstraction emerges from the move.
snippet: features/export/{route.py, service.py, query.py, tests/} -> controllers/, services/, repositories/, tests/
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Move code purely because strict layering is always cleaner.
Treat directory shape as proof of architectural correctness.
Create shared base service/repository classes to justify the horizontal layers.
expected_decision_properties: Prefer the cohesive vertical slice in the current context.
Distinguish dependency direction from physical folder uniformity.
Recognize locality/navigation cost as a real quality dimension.
Allow horizontal/shared layers only when reuse, policy, or lifecycle boundaries become real.
unacceptable_reasoning: Every application must use controller/service/repository directories.
Vertical slices are inherently less modular.
Uniform folder structure always outweighs feature locality.
verification_expectations: Check whether any real cross-feature reuse or policy boundary is introduced.
revisit_when: Multiple features share stable service/persistence policy.
The vertical slice begins violating dependency boundaries.
Shared lifecycle/ownership requires a common module.
